Combining the totals in cells L2 and M2 should give me the total amount of raw parts needed both for shipping and building completed parts at this location. 
In case it helps I can explain how the sheet works and its purpose. The number in A2 is a raw part used among others to build completed parts. The bolded numbers at the top of row 1 are completed parts, and the parts under them are the raw parts that make them. The quantities to the right are basically how many completed parts are needed that day, thus how many of each raw part. B2:K2 also contains how many raw parts are shipping for other facilities to make their own completed parts, aside from what will be needed to build completed parts here at this one. That total is in L2, and that was easy. L2 and M2 together will tell me exactly how many raw parts will be needed for both shipping and for building completed parts here.

real_max_row = 0
real_max_col = 0

    for cell in row:
        if cell.value is not None:
            real_max_row = max(real_max_row, cell.row)
            real_max_col = max(real_max_col, cell.column)

print("Sheet:", ws.title)
print("Real used range:", real_max_row, real_max_col)

# Per instruction, completed-part/raw-part data begins at column O.
# Raw-part columns are paired with quantity columns immediately to the right.
start_col = ws["O1"].column

# Dynamically identify pair-start/raw-part columns from row 1.
pair_start_cols = []
for col in range(start_col, real_max_col):
    header = ws.cell(1, col).value
    next_header = ws.cell(1, col + 1).value
    if header is not None and next_header is None:
        pair_start_cols.append(col)

# Same-layout fallback: every other column from O onward
if not pair_start_cols:
    pair_start_cols = list(range(start_col, real_max_col, 2))

last_pair_start = max(pair_start_cols)

# Formula must search ALL rows of the raw-part columns, not just row 2.
data_first_row = 2
data_last_row = real_max_row

criteria_first = get_column_letter(start_col)
criteria_last = get_column_letter(last_pair_start)
qty_first = get_column_letter(start_col + 1)
qty_last = get_column_letter(last_pair_start + 1)

# SUMPRODUCT logic:
# 1) MOD(COLUMN(...)-COLUMN(first),2)=0 keeps only raw-part columns O,Q,S,...
# 2) raw-part range = A2 finds every occurrence of the part number
# 3) matching quantity range P,R,T,... is summed
formula = (
    f'=SUMPRODUCT('
    f'--(MOD(COLUMN(${criteria_first}${data_first_row}:${criteria_last}${data_last_row})'
    f'-COLUMN(${criteria_first}${data_first_row}),2)=0),'
    f'--(${criteria_first}${data_first_row}:${criteria_last}${data_last_row}=$A2),'
    f'IFERROR(${qty_first}${data_first_row}:${qty_last}${data_last_row}*1,0)'
    f')'
)

# Write only M2 as required
ws["M2"] = formula
ws["M2"].number_format = ws["L2"].number_format

# Ensure formula recalculates when opened
try:
    wb.calculation.fullCalcOnLoad = True
    wb.calculation.forceFullCalc = True
except Exception:
    pass

output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
wb.save(output_path)

# VERIFY: reopen saved workbook and manually recompute total from original data
saved_wb = load_workbook(output_path, data_only=False)
saved_ws = saved_wb[ws.title]
print("Saved M2 formula:", saved_ws["M2"].value)

target = ws["A2"].value
manual_total = 0
matches = []

        raw_part = ws.cell(row, col).value

            manual_total += numeric_qty

print("Target part:", target)
print("Matches:", matches)
print("Manual recomputed total:", manual_total)

from openpyxl import load_workbook
from openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter
from pathlib import Path

input_path = Path("/mnt/data/spreadsheet/50682/1_50682_input.xlsx")
output_path = Path("/mnt/data/outputs/50682_0_f5a61ebd/1_50682_output.xlsx")

# -----------------------------
# 1. INSPECT
# -----------------------------
wb = load_workbook(input_path, data_only=False)

# Use the named sheet when present; otherwise fall back to the active sheet.
ws = wb["PART LIST (2)"] if "PART LIST (2)" in wb.sheetnames else wb.active

# Determine the real used range from actual non-empty cells.
real_max_row = 0
real_max_col = 0
for row in ws.iter_rows():
    for cell in row:
        if cell.value is not None:
            real_max_row = max(real_max_row, cell.row)
            real_max_col = max(real_max_col, cell.column)

print(f"Workbook sheets: {wb.sheetnames}")
print(f"Working sheet: {ws.title}")
print(f"Real used range: rows 1:{real_max_row}, cols 1:{real_max_col}")

# Data columns for completed-part/raw-part pairs start at column O per the instruction.
start_col = ws["O1"].column

# Identify the completed-part/raw-part columns by using row 1:
# row 1 has completed-part headers in the raw-part columns, with the quantity column immediately to the right.
pair_starts = []
for c in range(start_col, real_max_col):
    header_here = ws.cell(row=1, column=c).value
    header_next = ws.cell(row=1, column=c + 1).value
    if header_here is not None and header_next is None:
        pair_starts.append(c)

# Fallback for same-layout files if row-1 header detection is sparse:
# use every other column from O through the last available complete pair.
if not pair_starts:
    pair_starts = list(range(start_col, real_max_col, 2))

if not pair_starts:
    raise ValueError("No raw-part / quantity column pairs could be identified from column O onward.")

last_pair_start = max(pair_starts)
if last_pair_start + 1 > real_max_col:
    raise ValueError("The last detected raw-part column has no quantity column to its right.")

criteria_start_col = start_col
criteria_end_col = last_pair_start
sum_start_col = start_col + 1
sum_end_col = last_pair_start + 1

criteria_start = get_column_letter(criteria_start_col)
criteria_end = get_column_letter(criteria_end_col)
sum_start = get_column_letter(sum_start_col)
sum_end = get_column_letter(sum_end_col)

print(f"Detected raw-part criteria range for row 2: {criteria_start}2:{criteria_end}2")
print(f"Detected quantity sum range for row 2: {sum_start}2:{sum_end}2")

# -----------------------------
# 2. SOLVE
# -----------------------------
# Formula logic:
# - Look across the raw-part columns starting at O.
# - Only include every other column, because the adjacent columns are quantities.
# - When a raw-part cell equals A2, sum the numeric quantity immediately to its right.
#
# IFERROR(...*1,0) safely turns numeric quantities into numbers and ignores text/blanks.
formula = (
    f'=SUMPRODUCT('
    f'--(MOD(COLUMN(${criteria_start}2:${criteria_end}2)-COLUMN(${criteria_start}2),2)=0),'
    f'--(${criteria_start}2:${criteria_end}2=$A2),'
    f'IFERROR(${sum_start}2:${sum_end}2*1,0)'
    f')'
)

ws["M2"] = formula

# Ask spreadsheet apps to recalculate formulas when opened.
try:
    wb.calculation.fullCalcOnLoad = True
    wb.calculation.forceFullCalc = True
except Exception:
    pass

output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
wb.save(output_path)

# -----------------------------
# 3. VERIFY
# -----------------------------
# Re-open the saved file and print the answer cell.
check_wb = load_workbook(output_path, data_only=False)
check_ws = check_wb[ws.title]

print(f"Saved M2 formula: {check_ws['M2'].value}")

# Manual recomputation from the original input workbook using the same detected layout.
input_wb_for_check = load_workbook(input_path, data_only=False)
input_ws_for_check = input_wb_for_check[ws.title]

target_part = input_ws_for_check["A2"].value
manual_total = 0

for c in pair_starts:
    part_value = input_ws_for_check.cell(row=2, column=c).value
    qty_value = input_ws_for_check.cell(row=2, column=c + 1).value

    if part_value == target_part:
        try:
            if qty_value is not None:
                manual_total += float(qty_value)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            pass

print(f"Target raw part in A2: {target_part}")
print(f"Manual total from matching raw-part columns and right-side quantities: {manual_total}")
print(f"Output saved to: {output_path}")
